tweets.text:
12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X

A lot of people I know are moving their posting from LinkedIn to X. When they ask me how I grew 80k followers on X in one year, here’s what I tell them:

1. LinkedIn is a stage. X is a party. First you find your crowd, then you listen to what they're already talking about. Don't start talking until you get it

2. You can't reach the C-suite directly. LinkedIn is a professional network, so you can go straight to decision makers. X doesn't work like that. You have to get mass attention first, and then the right people notice you

3. Post way more than you think. On LinkedIn, 3-5 posts a week counts as a lot. I posted 3 times a day on X for 6 months. Some founders I follow post 5 times a day. It's not that they're on X all day. They just don't overthink it

4. Make posting a reflex. If you spend too long on a post, you won't post. Whenever a thought comes up, post it right there. No planning, no scheduling, no waiting for the right time

5. It's a numbers game. Most posts won't do well. Maybe 1 in 10 will. Maybe 1 in 50 goes viral. That's normal

6. Half your posts should be reactions. LinkedIn is mostly “proactive content”. On X, at least at the start, half of what you post should be “reactive content”: replies, quote tweets, commentary on what others already said

7. Know the difference between a reply and a quote tweet. A reply is like a LinkedIn DM. It says "notice me." A quote tweet uses someone else's content to grow your own account

8. Fix your feed first. If you wanna talk about cybersecurity and your feed is all politics, you can't join the right conversations. Pick a few big names in your niche. See who they follow and who they engage with, and follow those people too. Like, bookmark and comment. After about a week your timeline will look totally different

9. Write like you're texting an acquaintance. Polish turns people off. Everyone's allergic to perfect AI-sounding writing. And please don't use AI or bots to write your replies. People can tell, and they might block you

10. Post the stuff that's obvious to you. Make a list of the top 10 questions customers, investors and your team ask you. That's where you're the expert. What seems too obvious to talk about is exactly what people want to hear

11. Post what you just said out loud. If you say something in real life and people go "huh, never thought of it that way," post it on your way back. Don't wait, you'll forget. You don't have to block out time to think of what to say. Just say what you've already said

12. Show your face, and don't sell yet. X is a wall of text, so video stands out. I just record myself on my laptop with something on the screen. People wanna know you're a real human, not AI slop. And until you have about 1,000 followers, don't promote your company. Share real opinions first. Later, when you repost company news, always add your own take, not PR speak.

Remember: people follow people, not companies

Ven was one of the earliest believers that we could use our then-current model to solve millenium prize problems.

There are a lot of brilliant people in the world, but being brilliant and also having correctly-placed confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that others don't think is possible is a very valuable thing and fairly rare.

I am grateful so many people at OpenAI have this combination.

tweets.text:
Oh, one thing about kids:

Most good things get a little less satisfying the 100th time you do them.

A quiet evening hanging out with your kids, even doing very mundane stuff, is in the rare category of something repetitive just getting better and better.

tweets.text:
I am thankful for a lot of things in life, but my family is the best thing that has ever happened to me.

The two most common things people said to me before having kids is that it's better than anyone can explain to you and it goes very fast; these are both true and I don't have much to add. But I am very grateful and I love them more than there is any way to explain.

Also I cannot really imagine life without Ollie and I think without his unwavering support and great advice I would have gone crazy by now.

🦃
tweets.summary_zh: 生活中我有很多值得感谢的事，但家人是我最珍贵的宝贝。很多人告诉我，养孩子的快乐超出想象，而且时间过得特别快，这两点我完全同意。我真的很感激他们，对他们的爱无法用言语表达。生活中有了Ollie（可能是他的孩子或宠物），他的支持和建议让我变得更加理智。🦃

tweets.text:
12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X

A lot of people I know are moving their posting from LinkedIn to X. When they ask me how I grew 80k followers on X in one year, here’s what I tell them:

1. LinkedIn is a stage. X is a party. First you find your crowd, then you listen to what they're already talking about. Don't start talking until you get it

2. You can't reach the C-suite directly. LinkedIn is a professional network, so you can go straight to decision makers. X doesn't work like that. You have to get mass attention first, and then the right people notice you

3. Post way more than you think. On LinkedIn, 3-5 posts a week counts as a lot. I posted 3 times a day on X for 6 months. Some founders I follow post 5 times a day. It's not that they're on X all day. They just don't overthink it

4. Make posting a reflex. If you spend too long on a post, you won't post. Whenever a thought comes up, post it right there. No planning, no scheduling, no waiting for the right time

5. It's a numbers game. Most posts won't do well. Maybe 1 in 10 will. Maybe 1 in 50 goes viral. That's normal

6. Half your posts should be reactions. LinkedIn is mostly “proactive content”. On X, at least at the start, half of what you post should be “reactive content”: replies, quote tweets, commentary on what others already said

7. Know the difference between a reply and a quote tweet. A reply is like a LinkedIn DM. It says "notice me." A quote tweet uses someone else's content to grow your own account

8. Fix your feed first. If you wanna talk about cybersecurity and your feed is all politics, you can't join the right conversations. Pick a few big names in your niche. See who they follow and who they engage with, and follow those people too. Like, bookmark and comment. After about a week your timeline will look totally different

9. Write like you're texting an acquaintance. Polish turns people off. Everyone's allergic to perfect AI-sounding writing. And please don't use AI or bots to write your replies. People can tell, and they might block you

10. Post the stuff that's obvious to you. Make a list of the top 10 questions customers, investors and your team ask you. That's where you're the expert. What seems too obvious to talk about is exactly what people want to hear

11. Post what you just said out loud. If you say something in real life and people go "huh, never thought of it that way," post it on your way back. Don't wait, you'll forget. You don't have to block out time to think of what to say. Just say what you've already said

12. Show your face, and don't sell yet. X is a wall of text, so video stands out. I just record myself on my laptop with something on the screen. People wanna know you're a real human, not AI slop. And until you have about 1,000 followers, don't promote your company. Share real opinions first. Later, when you repost company news, always add your own take, not PR speak.

Remember: people follow people, not companies

tweets.text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. tweets.text:
AI native teams will eventually force the surrounding organization to become AI native too.

Take software development. coding velocity is way up thanks to AI, while actual shipped products and business impact are unchanged in most companies. That’s cos the surrounding system of experimentation tooling, evaluation, launch processes, and gtm are outdated.

It’s like sticking a Ferrari engine in a sedan and racing it on Indian roads. The engine can rev faster but the car speed is limited by its system and environment.

AI native companies were built ground up for this new way of building and shipping. They’re also able to shed suboptimal processes faster.

Market forces will quickly force all companies to adapt or perish.

If you’re solving this for your company: map out your product lifecycle and rebuild it ground up - tooling, team structure, gtm, everything.

tweets.text:
Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work. 

The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing. 

Next, as this step itself becomes redundant or slows down what agents are capable of, we will be giving agents goals to optimize against and they’ll go off on and increasingly solve larger problems for us. 

This may at first blush look like something whose impact gets stuck with coding, but actually a large percentage of knowledge work may eventually just converge with this form factor due to the massive productivity gains that can be generated. Agents will use computers, leverage our existing tools or write new ones, and write code on the fly to solve larger swaths of knowledge work. 

So even if a task today doesn’t seem to be “coding” directly, the task may eventually fold into being coding adjacent. Manufacturing, architecture, life sciences, material sciences, cyber, and on and on.
 
One big hurdle in the way ultimately will be that much of this work remains non-verifiable, so humans will be even more in the loop than they are in coding. But the part that they can hand off will just get bigger and bigger over time as the models are more capable.

So in short, pay attention to coding and you’ll get a sense for where work is going.
tweets.summary_zh: 编程可以让我们看到未来工作的模样。最初，我们还需要自己做很多的研究和打字，但将来会有智能系统（智能代理）来帮助我们协调工作。随着这些系统变得越来越强大，我们将设定目标，让它们解决更复杂的问题。虽然现在有些工作看起来跟编程无关，但未来很多知识型工作会和编程有关系，因为这样能提高工作效率。不过，很多工作仍然难以验证，因此人类的参与仍然重要。总之，关注编程能让你更了解未来工作的方向。

America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl

美国如果只专注于开发最先进的AI模型，却无法满足其他国家对自主AI的需求，就可能在全球AI竞争中失败。各国希望能够在自己的土地上、自己的基础设施上运行AI模型，这样才能掌握自己的技术。

如果美国公司不能提供这样的解决方案，中国公司就会填补这个空白，一旦国家开始使用中国的AI模型和基础设施，后续的技术转移和投资就会变得困难。因此，美国的发展和支持开放模型（可以让很多公司自由使用的AI模型）显得特别重要，这样才有机会让更多国家选择使用美国的技术。我们需要既有先进的技术领导，又有全球的广泛采用，开放模型是实现这两者的关键。

This wouldn’t have sounded possible a year ago, but it’s becoming much more reasonable now that you can get 10X output gains based on the latest in AI model and harness progress. The result is that teams within the same company are driving very different levels of output based on how they’ve adopted AI.

This is a different phenomenon from other tech. Typically in the economy you think of technology adoption rates on a per firm basis, because the company generally adopts a relatively standardized approach to doing the new tech thing. tweets.text:
New research from Replit on scaling laws for agent swarms. 

We show that scaling the number of agents can yield dramatic performance gains, but unlike traditional scaling laws, more compute doesn't necessarily translate into better results, and how agents organize themselves matters.

- Given a fixed two-hour window, Opus 5.5 went from a 3.7x speedup on NumPy with one agent to 18.9x with 32 agents.

- GPT-6.2 Astra was the strongest solo agent but exhibited negative scaling beyond 8 agents.

- Models spontaneously developed different organizational structures. Decentralized swarms scaled better than those that relied on centralized coordination.

- The parallelizability of the problem was a strong predictor of swarm performance.

- Interestingly, individual model intelligence is a poor predictor of collective intelligence.

We’re also open-sourcing Optimization-Bench to advance research into this new dimension of inference-time scaling.

This is a pretty key insight. Services businesses are always held back by their ability to deliver outcomes to customers. 

That scaling essentially only could come from headcount, and no matter how much demand you saw, there was always a finite amount of talent you could get for the problem you were going after. Not to mention, the customer generally always wants the work done faster, at a lower price, or at a higher quality.

Agents entirely change the calculus here, because now we can scale output in a way that’s decoupled from the among of time that goes in. A single engineer can have the output of dozens of engineers before. A single designer can probably build out your entire design system and brand. And so on.

Well why isn’t this just all agents then? Because the key is to still have experts on the front end that actually can ensure the right outcomes are delivered from agents.

It’s likely that we’re going to see this in a wide variety of categories. You’ll see this in cyber security, advertising and marketing, legal, accounting, IT transformation, and a number of other historically people-only services industries.

It’s a great time if you’re starting one of these businesses, or if you have the capability to transform an existing one.

tweets.text:
Yes to all of this. As agents take on more and more long running project work, and you have swarms of agents that parallelize work against a goal, the agent harness and architecture for orchestration will have to evolve. 

One of the biggest shifts is how those agents collectively share their knowledge, keep track of the tasks, and also coordinate with human users. This in theory is technically straightforward, but there’s a ton of complexity to get right to ensure agents can both get access to the revenant resources without too much or little exposure.

There are a lot of lessons to pull from based on how people already do this kind of work together (people share their files, have computers to work with, community in chats and inboxes, and so on). But equally the primitives need to be able to enable this work at a throughput far higher than people, and in a world where agents can much more easily become a vector of security risk. 

Going to be super fun building out this next generation of how agents operate. Lots of opportunity here both for horizontal and vertical specific approaches to bring this to life.
tweets.summary_zh: 越来越多的智能系统（代理）需要协作来完成长时间的项目，这就要求我们改进如何管理和组织这些系统的方式。其中一个主要变化是这些代理如何分享知识、跟踪任务，并与人类用户协调。尽管技术上看起来简单，但实际上面临很多复杂性，比如确保代理可以有效获取所需资源而不带来安全风险。未来的工作会很有趣，充满了机会来探索更高效的解决方案。

tweets.text:
This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math. We’re entering an era where solving problems will look very different from how we solved them in the past.

“This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.”

It used to be the case that to solve a particular problem - code, life sciences, math, cyber, engineering, and so on - you were ultimately bound by how much information an individual or team could retain and understand about the space. More information or more team members don’t always help, because it gets harder to connect the dots or coordinate amongst everyone. AI changes that completely. 

For the first time ever we can decouple the human context limits and ability to work through information from our ability to drive productivity or discoveries. This is likely not just a small increase in the kinds of discoveries we can drive, but a qualitative shift in human output. 

Now every single form of prior art, insight, past research, past decision, or unrelated breakthrough, can be used for the discovery or creation of something new. This is useful for anything from cybersecurity to life sciences research. Agents will be able to correlate entirely unrelated work to a separate project; scan every bit of data in your enterprise for solving a problem; and so on. 

The solutions may not be as elegant as they were in the past, but we sure will have far more of them. We’re only in the first couple of months of actually understanding the implications of this but it’s clearly going to drive a lot of change.
tweets.summary_zh: 最近的一个数学突破可能会改变我们解决问题的方式，不仅仅是数学领域。以前，解决问题主要依赖于人类的理解和团队的合作，但现在有了人工智能（AI），我们可以把这些限制打破，让机器帮助我们找到更多、更复杂的解决方案。虽然这些解决方案可能不如以前优雅，但数量会大大增加，对各个领域都非常有帮助，比如网络安全和生命科学研究。总之，未来的发现和创造将会与以往大不相同。

tweets.text:
This year we’ve had a clear jump in model capability where instead of telling agents precisely what to do, it’s better to use these systems to solve problems you can’t easily define yourself. 

A year ago you’d need to very clearly tell agents the how to design and develop your product idea, or there was almost no chance of success. Now, increasingly, the agent likely can come up with a better implementation than you’d have thought of because you can have it connect the dots between a far greater solution space than you can. 

This will be increasingly true in basically every domain of kneeler work. We’re going to see this impact in finance, legal, life sciences, cyber, and many other spaces where no person can hold onto all the available relevant industry knowledge to think of the best solution. 

Ultimately this is going to reshape our relationship with AI and how we deploy agents in our work. It won’t be about explicitly telling them, but instead giving them goals and enough freedom to pursue them in the best way they can.
tweets.summary_zh: 今年，AI模型的能力有了很大提升，我们不用再详细指示它们该怎么做，而是让它们帮助解决那些我们自己难以明确的问题。以前我们必须清晰地告诉AI怎么设计和开发产品，但现在AI能提出比我们更好的解决方案，因为它可以整合的信息比我们想象的要多得多。这个趋势将在金融、法律、生命科学等多个领域大显身手，改变我们与AI的关系，未来我们只需给它们设定目标，让它们自由去探索最佳解决方案。

tweets.text:
As these network attacks and impersonation attempts happen, who's securing the elderly? 

Especially thinking about my parents and grandparents.

There are four layers I can think through where this could work.

One is at the browser level, where somebody builds a secure browser that ensures that whatever websites they're going to are secured. Texts typically lead to a link, even for payments. This is why browser is key.

Two could be at the network layer, where there is a physical device, similar to Pi-hole, or an Onavo-like VPN on your phone, that blocks websites that could be deemed unsafe.

Three could be at the payments layer, where transactions that look like scams get flagged before the money leaves.

And fourth and most crazy could be at the phone level, where everything is monitored, and you're only getting calls from your loved ones. Cloned voices would work with a provider like Reality Defender. 

There are individual solutions for this today but none neatly packaged. 

This could all be packaged with insurance that covers any activities on the OS or phone. In that way, incentives are aligned to keep this on the edge.

The buyer would be the kids, someone like me, who get alerted when something looks off.
tweets.summary_zh: 在网络攻击和冒充行为越来越多的情况下，谁来保护老人呢？作者提出了一些想法，比如开发安全浏览器、使用物理设备屏蔽危险网站，以及在支付时识别诈骗交易，甚至可以监控电话，只接家人的来电。虽然现在有一些单独的解决方案，但还没有一个完整的产品来保护他们，可能还可以和保险结合，让买家（比如子女）及时收到警报。

podcasts.summary_zh:
视频讨论了Take-Two的首席执行官关于《GTA 7》开发的看法，强调此时推出新作还为时尚早，可能会影响其质量。CEO表示希望在未来能够给玩家带来更好的体验，因此在开发过程中需要更多的时间和资源。

💡 值得一看 — 这个视频提供了关于游戏行业开发周期的见解，能让你从中汲取如何平衡创意与市场需求的灵感，尤其对于TexTale在电商运营及品牌营销上的策略有启发。

producthunt.name: Alsona
producthunt.tagline: AI agents that turn buying signals into booked sales calls
producthunt.summary_zh: Alsona 是一种人工智能代理，能够识别潜在客户的购买信号，并将这些信号转化为预约的销售电话。它通过分析客户行为，有效提高销售转化率。

producthunt.name: beacon.sh
producthunt.tagline: Open-source self-improving memory for AI coding agents
producthunt.summary_zh: Beacon.sh 是一个开源的自我提升记忆系统，专为人工智能编程助手设计。它能够帮助 AI 在执行任务时记住先前的知识和经验，从而提高编程效率和准确性。通过不断自我学习和更新，Beacon.sh 可以适应用户的需求，变得更加智能。

producthunt.name: Wanaka Studio
producthunt.tagline: Make and publish 3D games with the first AI game engine
producthunt.summary_zh: Wanaka Studio是一款首个基于人工智能的游戏引擎，让用户能够轻松制作和发布3D游戏。它提供了简单易用的工具，用户无需编程经验也能创建出精彩的游戏。

producthunt.name: Empacer
producthunt.tagline: The voice-first assistant for small and medium businesses
producthunt.summary_zh: Empacer 是一款专为小企业主设计的语音助手。它能通过语音指令帮助用户管理日常任务，提升工作效率，并提供实时信息和建议。用户可以用更便捷的方式进行日常运营和决策。

producthunt.name: Screen Studio 4.0
producthunt.tagline: Glass Loupe, Camera Cutout, Edit by Transcript, and more
producthunt.summary_zh: Screen Studio 4.0是一款多功能屏幕录制和编辑软件。它提供透视镜、摄像头切割、逐字稿编辑等功能，用户可以轻松录制视频并进行后期处理。该软件旨在提升视频制作的效率和质量。

producthunt.name: RankSpot
producthunt.tagline: Pay-as-you-go SEO and AI Search execution layer for agents
producthunt.summary_zh: RankSpot 是一款按需付费的搜索引擎优化（SEO）和人工智能搜索执行平台。它助力代理商优化网站排名，提升搜索引擎的表现，让用户更容易找到相关信息。通过灵活的付费模式，用户可以根据实际需要使用工具和服务。

producthunt.name: Product Hunt MCP
producthunt.tagline: The community you trust in the assistant you use
producthunt.summary_zh: Product Hunt MCP是一个结合社区和助手功能的平台。用户可以在这里发现最新的产品和技术，同时获得来自社区的真实反馈和建议。它帮助用户更有效地找到有价值的工具和资源。

producthunt.name: Scalekit
producthunt.tagline: MCP gateway for production agents that acts on your behalf
producthunt.summary_zh: Scalekit 是一种 MCP 网关，用于生产代理，能够代表用户自动执行任务。它简化了管理和协调流程，提升了工作效率。通过 Scalekit，用户可以更轻松地监控和管理系统。

producthunt.name: TheBold
producthunt.tagline: Turn execution into meetings with investors
producthunt.summary_zh: TheBold是一款专为创业公司设计的工具，旨在帮助用户将执行任务转化为与投资者的会议。通过该平台，用户可以更高效地安排会议、展示项目进展，并促进与投资者的沟通与合作。

producthunt.name: Creatify Max
producthunt.tagline: Your ad teammate, from strategy to creation to launch
producthunt.summary_zh: Creatify Max是一款全面的广告助手，能够帮助用户从广告策略的制定到创意设计，再到最终的发布，提供全流程的支持。它简化了广告制作过程，让用户更轻松地打造高效的广告campaign。

producthunt.name: Plurai Simulation
producthunt.tagline: A simulated world that makes your agent improve on every run
producthunt.summary_zh: Plurai Simulation 是一个虚拟模拟环境，旨在帮助智能体在每次运行中不断学习和提升。通过反复训练，这个产品可以优化智能体的决策能力和表现。

producthunt.name: Hub
producthunt.tagline: Run 100 Claude Code or Codex sessions like 5
producthunt.summary_zh: Hub是一款高效的代码运行平台，能够以较少的资源同时运行多达100个Claude Code或Codex会话。它简化了开发流程，让用户能够更快地测试和迭代代码。通过Hub，用户可以更灵活地管理多个项目。

producthunt.name: Rakazo
producthunt.tagline: The open source Grok Bot alternative you actually own
producthunt.summary_zh: Rakazo是一款开源的Grok Bot替代品，用户可以完全掌控其源代码和功能。它可以帮助用户轻松创建和管理聊天机器人，支持自定义和扩展，以满足各种需求。用户无需依赖第三方平台，可以随时修改和维护自己的机器人。

producthunt.name: Templify AI
producthunt.tagline: Powerful content editor for people who aren’t editors
producthunt.summary_zh: Templify AI 是一款强大的内容编辑工具，专为非专业编辑人员设计。它能帮助用户轻松创建和优化各种类型的内容，无需复杂的编辑技能。通过智能模板和简洁的操作界面，用户可以快速生成高质量的文章和报告。

producthunt.name: Tobira Site Agent
producthunt.tagline: Turn your website into an AI agent that sells to AI agents
producthunt.summary_zh: Tobira Site Agent 是一个将您的网站转变为智能代理的工具。它能够自动与其他智能代理互动，帮助您在线销售产品或服务。通过这个平台，您可以实现更高效的自动化交易。

github_trending.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 85 skills, 16 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个为寻找软件漏洞和进行安全测试而设计的工具包，包含了很多实用的技能和命令，可以帮助团队识别和修复安全问题。对于Yves的业务，特别是Logic Labs（AI公司），这个项目可以提供重要的安全保障，帮助提升其产品的安全性和可信度，让其在 AI 应用方面更具竞争力。同时，对他作为创意设计从业者来说，可以借鉴其系统化的方法论，提升在产品设计中的风险评估和管理能力。

github_trending.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一种有效的技能框架和软件开发方法，旨在帮助团队更高效地协作与创造。对于Yves而言，这个项目可以为Logic Labs提供更好的软件开发流程支持，提升AI项目的创新能力，同时也能为TexTale在技术驱动的电商运营中提供参考，帮助他更好地整合创意与科技。作为创意设计从业者，这个框架也能激发他的创意思维，提高设计效率。
这个项目旨在让所有软件都能通过命令行界面进行智能操作，提升用户与软件之间的互动效率。对于Yves来说，这个项目可能对Logic Labs（AI 公司）更有帮助，因为它能够增强AI在软件开发中的应用，提升团队的工作效率和创意实现。此外，作为创意设计从业者，他也可以借助这个项目提高设计工具的智能化水平，更好地满足市场需求。

github_trending.description: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.
github_trending.summary_zh:
这个项目允许用户在短短两小时内，从零开始训练一个64MB的大型语言模型。它提供了一种简便的方法，帮助用户快速构建和定制自己的AI模型。

对于Yves来说，这个项目对Logic Labs（AI公司）非常有帮助，可以加速AI应用的开发和实验。同时，它也为TexTale的品牌营销和产品推荐等方面提供了创新的AI工具，提升了客户的购物体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves可以利用这个工具探索新的设计理念和创意表达方式。

github_trending.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目主要是为Cursor提供插件规范和官方插件，使开发者能够创建和共享插件，从而扩展Cursor的功能。对Yves来说，这个项目可以帮助Logic Labs在AI领域更好地整合和开发工具，同时也能为TexTale提供更多的创意设计和电商运营支持，例如通过定制插件提升用户体验和品牌互动。

github_trending.description: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一种知识基础设施，通过一个API让用户能够搜索、抓取和访问超过550个数据提供者的数据，从而提升智能代理的能力。针对Yves，Logic Labs可能会从中受益，因为它可以帮助开发更智能的AI应用，改善数据获取和分析能力；同时，对于TexTale，利用这些数据可以更好地了解市场趋势和消费者行为，从而优化电商运营和品牌营销策略。

github_trending.description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是NGINX的开源代码库，主要用于提供高性能的Web服务器和反向代理服务，可以帮助网站处理大量的访问请求。对于Yves来说，NGINX可以为TexTale的电商平台提供稳定快速的访问体验，提升用户的购物体验，同时也能为Logic Labs在处理AI模型部署时提供支持，确保数据传输的高效和安全。此外，作为创意设计从业者，了解这样高效的技术工具可以帮助他更好地进行项目的规划和实施。

github_trending.description: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
github_trending.summary_zh: OpenVINO™ 是一个开源工具包，旨在优化和部署人工智能推理，这意味着它可以帮助加速 AI 模型在不同设备上的应用，使其更高效地工作。对 Yves 来说，这个项目可以为 Logic Labs 提供更强大的 AI 技术支持，提升 AI 模型的性能和部署效率，同时也能为 TexTale 的产品创新提供技术基础，助力更智能的电商体验。作为创意设计从业者，Yves 还可以利用 OpenVINO 优化AI应用，使其在设计和用户体验上更加出色。

github_trending.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, Qoder, and Pi. 52 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目提供了一套用于创建图表的设计工具，支持多种类型的图表，使用简单的 HTML 和 SVG 格式，可以方便地用于高质量的视觉呈现。对于Yves来说，这个工具非常适合Logic Labs，在AI行业中进行创意思维的可视化表达，同时也能够帮助TexTale在产品展示和营销中使用精美图表提升吸引力，增强品牌形象。作为一名创意设计从业者，这个项目能够丰富他的设计工具箱，提高工作效率和创作灵感。

github_trending.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
github_trending.summary_zh: 这个项目是一个人工智能助手，可以帮助用户在多个平台（如Reddit、X、YouTube等）上研究任何话题，并为其提供一个经过综合整理的总结。对于Yves而言，这个项目对Logic Labs（AI公司）非常有帮助，因为它可以增强其AI工具的研究与分析能力，进而提升创意设计的深度和广度。
